key_insight: The paper argues that in auditable, hypothesis-driven decision tasks, output discipline and structured reasoning matter more than raw model scale, and a falsification-guided protocol can rescue weak models while exposing the limits of already-disciplined ones.
engineering_relevance: For dependable agent systems, the key design target is not only better models but enforceable output formats, explicit candidate-vs-evidence checking, and termination guarantees that make decisions machine-verifiable.
method: Five-stage closed-loop agent protocol for decision making
Candidate × evidence matrix with falsification of every candidate against every evidence item
License a conclusion only after at least half the candidates are falsified and survivors are emitted in a single-line verifiable format
evidence_signal: On TCMEval-SDT (200 cases), the protocol improved weak models by about +0.27, reduced one model’s run-to-run standard deviation from 0.218 to 0.007, and transferred to misinformation-robust math reasoning with 89.8% recall and 6.8% false-positive rate.
watch_item: The protocol can reduce accuracy on already disciplined models, so implementation should be budget-aware and benchmarked against format overhead and task-specific failure modes.
paper_title: Output Discipline Sets the Floor: A Falsification-Guided, Model-Agnostic Agent Protocol for Auditable Hypothesis-Driven Decision Making
